name: White Gingerbread
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: quarters of a pound of butter
ingredients.originalText: three quarters of a pound of butter

ingredients.name: common white sugar powdered
ingredients.originalText: a pound of common white sugar powdered

ingredients.name: the best white ginger
ingredients.originalText: three table-spoonfuls of the best white ginger

ingredients.name: wine glass of sour milk
ingredients.originalText: a wine glass of sour milk

instructions.text: Sift two pounds of flour into a deep pan, and rub into it three quarters of a pound of butter
Mix in a pound of common white sugar powdered and three table-spoonfuls of the best white ginger
Beat four eggs very light, and mix them gradually with the other ingredients in the pan
Add a small tea-spoonful of pearl-ash melted in a wine glass of sour milk
Stir the whole as hard as possible
Flour your paste-board and lay the lump of dough upon it
Roll it out into a sheet an inch thick, adding more flour if necessary
Butter a large shallow square pan and lay the dough into it
Bake it in a moderate oven
When cold, cut it into squares, or cut it out into separate cakes with a jagging iron previous to baking
Do not lay them too close together in the pan, lest they run into each other

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Sift two pounds of flour into a deep pan, and rub into it three quarters of a pound of butter
2. Mix in a pound of common white sugar powdered and three table-spoonfuls of the best white ginger
3. Beat four eggs very light, and mix them gradually with the other ingredients in the pan
4. Add a small tea-spoonful of pearl-ash melted in a wine glass of sour milk
5. Stir the whole as hard as possible
6. Flour your paste-board and lay the lump of dough upon it
7. Roll it out into a sheet an inch thick, adding more flour if necessary
8. Butter a large shallow square pan and lay the dough into it
9. Bake it in a moderate oven
10. When cold, cut it into squares, or cut it out into separate cakes with a jagging iron previous to baking
11. Do not lay them too close together in the pan, lest they run into each other
